title: Pasta alla Trapanese
subtitle: Sicilian spaghetti with a raw almond and tomato pesto
excerpt: Spaghetti tossed in a raw, pounded pesto of almonds, cherry tomatoes, basil, and pecorino. No cooking for the sauce. Everything comes together in the time the pasta takes to boil.
sourceNotes: Sicilian summer pasta from the province of Trapani. A cousin of Ligurian pesto, using almonds and tomato in place of pine nuts.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pesto can be made 2 hours ahead and kept covered at room temperature. Do not refrigerate or the tomatoes turn mealy.

content.text: Pasta alla trapanese uses a raw pesto: no cooking, no blender needed if you have a pestle and mortar. The sauce is coarse and bright. Keep it that way.

items.prepNote: finely grated, plus extra to serve

content.text: Bring a large saucepan of well-salted water to a rolling boil.
Pound the garlic and salt flakes to a paste in the pestle and mortar. Add the almonds and pound to a rough, crumbly texture. Do not grind to a powder.
Add the basil leaves and pound briefly until bruised and broken down but not completely smooth.
Add the cherry tomato halves. Crush them roughly into the mixture. You want a chunky sauce, not a puree.
Stir in the olive oil, grated pecorino, black pepper, and chilli flakes if using. Taste and adjust salt.
Cook the spaghetti according to the packet. Reserve a large mug of pasta cooking water before draining. Drain the pasta.
Transfer the drained pasta to the large bowl. Add the pesto and toss well. Add a splash of pasta water if the sauce looks too thick. Serve immediately with extra pecorino.

items.symptom: The pesto is too stiff and does not coat the pasta.
items.cause: Not enough oil or the tomatoes were under-ripe and dry.
items.fix: Stir in a splash of pasta cooking water and a little more olive oil until the sauce flows easily.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes sharp and thin.
items.cause: The tomatoes were watery or very acidic.
items.fix: Add an extra tablespoon of grated pecorino and a pinch of salt. The cheese rounds out the acidity.

items.symptom: The almonds are too hard and crunchy in the sauce.
items.fix: Return the pesto to the mortar and pound further until the almonds are broken into sand-grain-sized pieces.
